summary:
The Highland Splitfin (*Hubbsina turneri*) is a small freshwater fish that once threaded through the lakes, rivers, and springs of Michoacán, Mexico — a landscape of highland waters now dramatically transformed. Adapted to the endorheic drainages of the Río Grande de Morelia system, this delicate species belonged to an ancient family of livebearers found nowhere else on Earth.

Its world has been steadily erased. The great Zacapu wetland, once sprawling across 33,500 hectares, has been drained to just 33.5 — a loss of 99% — to make way for farmland. Pollution and sedimentation have done the rest. A last-known spring dried up entirely. Today, the Highland Splitfin persists only in Lago Zacapu, holding on at the very edge of existence.
